about.label: About
about.heading: Khao Sok National Park — Southern Thailand's Wild Heart
about.entityIntro: Welcome to Khao Sok National Park — widely known simply as Khao Sok. In Surat Thani Province, Southern Thailand, this destination serves as a primary hub for travellers visiting the region.
about.lead: A 739 km² sanctuary of primeval rainforest, hidden lakes and some of Southeast Asia's richest wildlife
about.paragraph1: Khao Sok National Park covers about 739 km² in Surat Thani Province, Southern Thailand. Established in 1980 as the country's 22nd national park, it protects one of the oldest rainforests on Earth — its ecosystem is estimated to be around 160 million years old, far older than the Amazon.
about.paragraph2: At its centre lies Cheow Lan Lake (ทะเลสาบเชี้ยวหลาน), a vast emerald reservoir created in the early 1980s when the Ratchaprapha Dam flooded a hidden valley. Today the lake's limestone karsts rise straight from the water, sheltering gibbons, hornbills and — with luck — wild elephants.
about.quote: Stand still on the lake at dawn and the only sound is the call of a gibbon echoing across 160 million years of forest.

highlights.title: One of Earth's oldest
highlights.desc: A rainforest some scientists date to 160 million years — older than the Amazon and rich with rare plants

highlights.desc: A 165 km² emerald reservoir of limestone karsts and floating raft-house lodges

highlights.title: Rare & endangered
highlights.desc: Home to elephants, gibbons, tapirs, hornbills and the giant Rafflesia kerrii flower

editorTip.text: Stay at least one night on a lake raft house — dawn mist on the karsts is unforgettable

eco.label: Ecology
eco.heading: Ancient Rainforest & Karst Ecosystem
eco.quote: Few places on Earth pack so many life forms into one valley — from pitcher plants to prehistoric ferns.
eco.intro: Khao Sok sits where two monsoon systems meet, making it one of the wettest and most biologically intense places in Thailand. The lowland evergreen rainforest climbs into limestone mountains (โควาหินปูน), while the lake adds a unique aquatic habitat.

checklist.title: 🌿 Fauna & Flora Checklist
checklist.intro: Take this checklist to Khao Sok and log your encounters with the rainforest's residents:

items.name: Great Hornbill
items.best: Year-round · best at dawn/dusk in the canopy

items.name: Lar Gibbon
items.best: Heard year-round · morning calls by the lake

micro.title: Two monsoons
micro.desc: Both the southwest (May–Oct) and northeast (Nov–Feb) winds bring rain, so the forest stays lush almost year-round.

micro.title: Cloud-catching peaks
micro.desc: Mist clings to the karsts daily, dripping moisture that feeds countless ferns, mosses and orchids.

micro.title: Carbon-rich old growth
micro.desc: Unbroken ancient forest stores vast carbon and shelters species found almost nowhere else.

plants.title: Rafflesia kerrii — the giant flower
plants.desc: Thailand's largest flower (up to 80 cm across) blooms briefly on forest vines; a true Khao Sok specialty.

items.name: Peak bloom (Nov–Mar)
items.desc: Seen with a certified guide leading you deep into the forest; in the rainy season trails are muddy and most Rafflesia are only buds or already decayed — not the best time to see them.

items.name: Pitcher plants & orchids
items.desc: Hill streams hide Nepenthes pitcher plants; trunks wear epiphytic orchids and ferns.

plants.title: Primary rainforest giants
plants.desc: Towering dipterocarps, palms and rattan form layered canopy, understory and forest floor.

items.name: Wild bananas & gingers
items.desc: Shady trails glow with wild ginger flowers and begonias.

items.name: Bamboo & rattan
items.desc: Dense thickets that shelter small mammals and birds.

plants.title: Limestone cliff flora
plants.desc: Sheer karst walls host unique ferns and fig trees whose fruits draw hornbills and gibbons.

wildlife: Mammals: Asian elephant, Malayan tapir, gaur, leopard, dhole and several gibbon species roam the deeper forest
Birds: hornbills (great, wreathed, bushy-crested), broadbills, kingfishers and migratory species over the lake
Reptiles & amphibians: monitor lizards, reticulated pythons and a chorus of frogs after rain
eco.lntIntro: This is a fragile, protected rainforest — small actions keep it wild for the next visitor.
lnt: Stay on trails and boardwalks; never pick Rafflesia, orchids or any plant
Take all rubbish out — there is no bin on the lake or deep trails
Keep quiet on night safaris and never feed or approach wildlife

history.label: History
history.heading: History & Significance of Khao Sok National Park
history.intro: From ancient rainforest to modern national park — and a lost valley now beneath the lake

blocks.title: 250 Million Years Ago — An Ancient Ocean Reef
blocks.text: The steep karst limestone peaks of Khao Sok are not ordinary mountains — they were once a vast coral reef in the Permian ocean 250 million years ago. Tectonic uplift raised them, and millions of years of rain carved them into the 'underwater Ha Long Bay' we see today.

blocks.title: 160 Million Years — An Eternal Rainforest
blocks.text: When ice ages reshaped the planet, Khao Sok's position between two monsoon systems spared it from drought, leaving one of Earth's oldest, unbroken evergreen rainforests — estimated at around 160 million years old, older than the Amazon.

blocks.title: The 1970s — A Forest Sheltered by History
blocks.text: Between 1975 and 1982, Khao Sok's deep jungle and caves (such as Ai Po Cave) served as a hidden base for student activists and guerrillas. The military standoff that followed unexpectedly sealed off the area, keeping out commercial loggers and miners and miraculously sparing this ancient rainforest from the wholesale deforestation of 1970s Southeast Asia.

blocks.title: 1980 — National Park & the Dam
blocks.text: In December 1980, Khao Sok became Thailand's 22nd national park. Soon after, the Ratchaprapha Dam was built; its rising waters created the ~165 km² emerald Cheow Lan Lake, turning a hidden valley into a stunning watery maze.

legend.title: 📜 Place-name Legend: From 'Mountain of Corpses' to 'Mountain of Hair'
legend.text: The name 'Khao Sok' comes from a sorrowful past. In the late 19th century (or 1944, by some accounts), a severe epidemic (cholera/smallpox) ravaged local villages. The mountain was first named 'Khao Sop' (เขาศพ, 'Mountain of Corpses'). Later, to invite good fortune and dispel the gloom, locals changed the pronunciation to 'Khao Sok' (เขาสก, 'forest as lush and long as flowing hair'). Elders still believe the ancient village temples submerged by the dam guard the waters of Cheow Lan Lake, and that on calm mornings you may hear their serene bells ringing softly from below the surface.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: Khao Sok's rainforest is around 160 million years old — older than the Amazon — and its limestone peaks that rise from the water are actually 250-million-year-old Permian coral reefs. It is also home to one of the world's largest flowers, the Rafflesia kerrii.

twoZone.title: Two Zones: Don't Go to the Wrong One
twoZone.intro: First-time visitors often confuse the 'Park HQ' with 'Cheow Lan Lake'. The two are about 50 km apart and offer very different experiences:

items.name: Zone 1 · Main Park HQ (Phanom)
items.suits: Jungle trekking, waterfalls, Rafflesia spotting, tree-house stays
items.desc: In Phanom District, Surat Thani, postcode 84250. Land-based rainforest, trails, waterfalls and jungle lodges.

items.name: Zone 2 · Cheow Lan Lake (Ban Ta Khun)
items.suits: Long-tail boat trips, floating raft houses, limestone karsts (Three Sisters), cave visits
items.desc: In Ban Ta Khun District, postcode 84230. Reach it by boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam — the heart of the lake scenery and floating stays.

items.label: Boats on Cheow Lan Lake
items.value: No sailings before sunrise or after sunset

items.label: Night activities
items.value: HQ zone only, with a guide

fees.title: National Park Entrance Fee

items.title: Foreign visitors — lake zone (Ratchaprapha Dam)
items.desc: Adult 300 THB / child 150 THB — the rate most lake visitors pay

items.title: Foreign visitors — park standard (DNP rate group 2)
items.desc: Adult 200 THB / child 100 THB

items.title: Thai nationals
items.desc: Adult 40 THB / child 20 THB

items.title: Child rate applies to
items.desc: Ages 3–14, or height up to 140 cm

fees.note: Fees are set by the Department of National Parks (DNP) and paid in cash at the checkpoint. Khao Sok is in DNP rate group 2; the Ratchaprapha Dam / Cheow Lan Lake zone has been designated a special-fee area since 1 May 2024. If prices change, the on-site notice at the checkpoint prevails.

items.title: From Surat Thani
items.desc: The park HQ (Phanom District) is about 110–120 km (1.5–2 hrs' drive) west (south-west) of Surat Thani city; the Ratchaprapha Dam pier for Cheow Lan Lake (Ban Ta Khun District) is about 60–65 km west. Buses, minivans and taxis connect the city, railway station and park.

items.title: From Phuket / Krabi
items.desc: Roughly 2.5–3 hrs by road; many combine Khao Sok with Andaman coast trips.

items.title: Lake & dam transfer
items.desc: The Ratchaprapha Dam (gateway to Cheow Lan Lake) is ~1 hr from the park HQ; most lake tours include transfer.

items.title: From the airport
items.desc: Surat Thani Airport (URT) is ~70 km away; Phuket (HKT) and Krabi (KBV) are 2.5–3 hrs. Pre-book a van or join a tour.

photography.title: Photography & Lake Guide
photography.intro: Khao Sok is a photographer's dream: misty karsts at dawn, glassy lake reflections and wildlife in low light.

times.desc: Dawn mist on the lake — soft light, glassy water and the iconic karst silhouettes. Best for raft-house sunrise shots.
Clearer skies; good for trekking photos, waterfalls and wildlife along the trails.
Golden light on the limestone cliffs; the lake turns amber before sunset.

spots.name: Cheow Lan Lake at dawn
spots.view: Limestone karsts mirrored in still water — the postcard shot of Khao Sok.
spots.tip: Shoot from a raft house or long-tail boat at first light; use a wide lens and a polariser to deepen the emerald water.

spots.name: Nam Talu Cave mouth
spots.view: Dramatic limestone gorge where a cool stream meets the jungle.
spots.tip: Bring a waterproof bag; long exposure on the flowing stream gives silky water.

spots.name: Jungle trek viewpoint
spots.view: Canopy walkways and ridges open onto valley panoramas.
spots.tip: Use a telephoto to compress layers of mist and forest.

settings.camera: Shutter 1/4s–1s · f/8–f/11 · ISO 100 · tripod + ND filter
settings.phone: iPhone: shoot Live Photo then 'Long Exposure'. Android: Pro mode, shutter 0.5s–1s.
Tap the subject to focus; use 2×–5× zoom and burst mode for birds.

tips: Humidity is extreme — pack silica gel and a dry bag for cameras and phones.
A polariser is the karst cheat: it cuts glare on water and deepens the emerald tones.
Leeches are common on wet trails — wear long socks and check legs after treks.
Boats move; brace your camera or use faster shutter to avoid blur on the lake.

bestTime.title: Best Season
bestTime.intro: Khao Sok has two broad seasons. The dry window is most comfortable; the green season is lushest.

seasons.name: Best weather · Easier trekking
seasons.desc: Lower rainfall, clearer trails and calm lake water — the most popular and comfortable time, though still humid. Book raft houses ahead.

seasons.name: Lush & wild · Wildlife active
seasons.desc: Heavy monsoon rain fills the lake and makes vegetation lush — also the most spectacular waterfalls and active wildlife. But trails flood easily and leeches thrive, and this is NOT the Rafflesia peak (that is the dry season, Nov–Mar). Bring proper rain gear.

items.title: Leeches & insects
items.desc: Wet forest means leeches and mosquitoes — use repellent and cover up on treks.

items.title: Boat & lake safety
items.desc: Always wear a life jacket on long-tail boats; weather on the lake can change fast.

items.title: Wild elephants
items.desc: Never approach or feed elephants; keep a safe distance and follow your guide.

accessibility.title: Accessibility & Family Tips
accessibility.intro: The park HQ and lake pier are easy to reach, though deep jungle treks are rugged.

items.title: Easy HQ access
items.desc: The visitor centre, restaurants and boat pier are near the road with parking and toilets.

items.title: Gentle options
items.desc: Short nature trails and a boat cruise suit families and seniors; longer treks need fitness.

items.title: Facilities
items.desc: Shops, food stalls and lodges cluster near the entrance; avoid midday heat — go early or late.

nearby.title: Landmarks & Attractions Around Khao Sok
nearby.lead: When visiting Khao Sok National Park, visitors can easily explore surrounding landmarks and points of interest, including Cheow Lan Lake and Ratchaprapha Dam.

items.name: Cheow Lan Lake
items.desc: The emerald reservoir of limestone karsts and floating raft houses — Khao Sok's signature sight.

items.name: Ratchaprapha Dam
items.desc: The dam that created the lake, with viewpoints over the flooded valley.

items.name: Khlong Phanom National Park
items.desc: Adjacent rainforest with caves and waterfalls, great for quieter trekking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Khao Sok?
faqs.a: December to April is driest and most comfortable; May to November is lush and wildlife-rich but wet. The lake is beautiful year-round.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for trekking?
faqs.a: Short trails are self-guided, but jungle treks, caves and Rafflesia spotting require a certified guide, arranged at the park HQ.

faqs.q: Can I stay on Cheow Lan Lake?
faqs.a: Yes — floating raft-house lodges offer overnight stays with meals; most packages include boat transfer from the dam.

faqs.q: Is there an entrance fee?
faqs.a: Yes. Foreign visitors pay 200 THB (adult) / 100 THB (child) under DNP rate group 2, and the Ratchaprapha Dam / Cheow Lan Lake zone is a designated special-fee area at 300 THB (adult) / 150 THB (child) — the amount most lake visitors pay. Thai nationals pay 40/20 THB. Lake boats and raft houses are priced separately. If prices change, the on-site notice prevails.

faqs.q: How do I get there from the coast?
faqs.a: Phuket and Krabi are about 2.5–3 hours away by road; many visitors combine Khao Sok with an Andaman beach trip.

faqs.q: Where is Khao Sok National Park located?
faqs.a: Khao Sok National Park spans Phanom and Ban Ta Khun districts in Surat Thani Province, Southern Thailand. The main park HQ (Phanom District, postcode 84250) is about 110–120 km west of Surat Thani city, while the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam pier (Ban Ta Khun District, Khao Phang, postcode 84230) is about 60–65 km west. The two zones are ~50 km apart; the maps pin (Plus code XJHQ+37) marks the lake area.

faqs.q: Is Khao Sok National Park free to visit?
faqs.a: No. Foreign visitors pay 200 THB (adult) / 100 THB (child) at the park standard rate, or 300/150 THB in the Ratchaprapha Dam / Cheow Lan Lake special-fee zone. Thai nationals pay 40/20 THB. The park is open daily from 06:00 to 18:00; Cheow Lan Lake boat tours are priced separately. If prices change, the on-site notice prevails.

faqs.q: Can I visit Khao Sok National Park as a day trip?
faqs.a: Yes — a day trip is possible from Surat Thani, Phuket, Krabi or Khao Lak, but staying one night in a Cheow Lan Lake raft house is what most visitors remember most.

weather.sceneNote: Khao Sok is mostly lake, limestone ridge and rainforest trail — here's how each is affected today.

lake.name: Cheow Lan Lake · boats & raft houses
lake.ok: Calm water — great for long-tail boat trips and a night on a raft house.
lake.caution: Boat departures may be delayed or cancelled; confirm with your operator first.
lake.stop: Skip the lake today — long-tail boats are likely suspended.

hike.name: Limestone ridge · viewpoints
hike.ok: Clear views — a good day to climb for the mist and the panorama.
hike.caution: Windy and slippery rock up top; take extra care and add a layer.
hike.stop: High risk of lightning and flash flooding — stay off the summit and out of gorges.

forest.name: Rainforest trail · waterfalls
forest.ok: Cool shade — ideal for trails, birdwatching and hunting for Rafflesia.
forest.caution: Slippery trail with active leeches and mosquitoes; wear long trousers and socks.
forest.stop: Streams rise fast in heavy rain — stay out of the waterfall and valley trails.

rain60.outfit: Rain is likely — bring rain gear and wear quick-dry clothing.
rain60.plan: Prioritise indoor or sheltered plans; postpone forest hikes and lake cruises.

drizzle.outfit: Light rain — surfaces are slick, so watch your footing.
drizzle.plan: Outdoor activities will be less enjoyable; slow down on boardwalks and steps.

rainHeavy.risk: Heavy rainfall — avoid valleys, low ground and fast-rising streams.
rainHeavy.outfit: Wear a waterproof shell; skip cotton that soaks and clings.
rainHeavy.plan: Not a day for outdoor activities — boats and cable cars may be suspended; switch to indoor or vehicle-based plans.
rainHeavy.pack: Rain poncho (no long umbrellas in wind), dry bag

thunder.risk: Lightning risk — never swim on the lake, stand on summits or shelter under trees.
thunder.outfit: Take a waterproof shell and leave metal jewellery behind.
thunder.plan: Water activities and cave tours are likely closed; move to indoor activities.

wind56.plan: Lake cruises and some open-air activities may be suspended.
wind56.pack: Windproof jacket; hats will fly off, and loose long dresses are a bad idea.

wind7.risk: Strong wind — keep away from billboards, shoreline rocks and dead trees.
wind7.plan: Outdoor and lake activities will most likely be closed; rescheduling is safer.

hot.outfit: Hot — avoid heading out at midday and choose light, breathable clothing.
hot.plan: Shorten outdoor time and move hiking to early morning or late afternoon.
hot.pack: Sunscreen, plenty of water, heat relief basics

uv.plan: Stay in the shade or indoors around midday rather than lingering in the sun.

uvExtreme.risk: Extreme UV — exposed skin can burn within 20 minutes.

tempDiff.outfit: Big day–night temperature swing — pack a jacket you can add or remove.

cold.outfit: Chilly — dress warmly and keep your core covered.

humid.outfit: Hot and humid — quick-dry, breathable fabrics feel far better.

sunny.plan: Clear skies — excellent for outdoor exploring and for sunrise or sunset views.

cloudy.plan: Soft, even light — great for photos and for spending hours outdoors.

fog.risk: Low visibility — lake boats and flights are prone to delays.
fog.plan: Not a day for mountain or lake views; keep your schedule flexible.

wetTrail.plan: After rain the trail is slick and leeches are active — long trousers, long socks, slow steps.
wetTrail.pack: Insect repellent, long socks, grippy hiking shoes

sections.h: Where the lake is — and why it is not the park entrance
sections.p: Khao Sok National Park has two visitor zones about 50 km apart. The main park HQ in Phanom District (postcode 84250) is the land-based rainforest entrance, while Cheow Lan Lake lies in Ban Ta Khun District (postcode 84230) and is reached by boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam. Driving to the wrong one is the most common mistake visitors make.
list: Park HQ — jungle trails, waterfalls, Rafflesia spotting, tree-house lodges
Cheow Lan Lake — long-tail boats, limestone karsts, cave visits, floating raft houses
Both zones charge the national park entrance fee

sections.h: Day trip or overnight on a raft house?
sections.p: A day trip is possible, but the boat ride from the dam pier to the main raft-house area takes about an hour each way, so a large part of the day is spent travelling. Staying one night is what most visitors remember: mist on still water at dawn and the lake to yourself before the day-trippers arrive.
list: Day trip — boat cruise, a viewpoint stop and lunch, back at the pier by late afternoon
One night — raft house with meals, sunrise on the water and night jungle sounds
Two nights — adds kayaking, a jungle trek and a cave or waterfall stop

sections.p: Floating raft houses are operated by companies licensed for the lake and are sold as packages rather than as plain rooms. A typical package includes the boat transfer from the dam, meals, life jackets and a local guide; rates vary with the season and the standard of the raft, so confirm exactly what is included with your operator before paying.
list: Book well ahead in the dry season (Dec–Apr) and on Thai holiday weekends
Bring cash — card payment is rare on the lake
Power is usually generator-limited, so charging points and hot water may be restricted
Mobile signal becomes patchy once the boat leaves the pier

sections.p: The national park entrance fee is charged separately from the boat and raft-house package. The lake zone at Ratchaprapha Dam is a designated special-fee area, so foreign visitors pay 300 THB for adults and 150 THB for children; the park standard rate (DNP group 2) is 200 THB and 100 THB. Thai nationals pay 40 THB and 20 THB. Boat and raft-house prices are quoted per package, not per park ticket. If prices change, the on-site notice prevails.

Life jackets are mandatory on long-tail boats, and lake weather can turn quickly in the afternoon. Swim only from the raft house where staff can watch the water, keep children within reach, and stay out of the water during and after heavy rain.
list: Wear the life jacket for the whole crossing
Do not swim far from the raft house — the reservoir is deep and drops away quickly
Cave visits such as Nam Talu run in the dry season only and must be guided; they are closed when flash-flood risk is high
There is no night boating and no night activity on the lake — keep transfers, swims and viewpoint stops inside daylight

sections.p: The lake is scenic all year, but the experience differs sharply. December to April brings calmer water, clearer trails and the best chance of the mirrored-karst photographs. May to November is the green season: the reservoir fills, the waterfalls run hard and the forest is at its lushest, but boat departures can be delayed and trails flood.
list: Dawn (roughly 06:30–08:30) is the golden window for mist and glassy water
Afternoon storms are common from May to November — plan boat transfers for the morning
Overnight stays sell out well in advance in the dry season

lake.faqTitle: Cheow Lan Lake: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: Can I get to Cheow Lan Lake without a tour?
faqs.a: Yes — drive to the Ratchaprapha Dam pier and hire a long-tail boat there, or book a raft house that includes the transfer. In practice most visitors book a package, because boats are shared and there is no reliable walk-up ticket window at the pier.

faqs.q: How long is the boat ride to the raft houses?
faqs.a: About one hour by long-tail boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam pier to the main raft-house area, depending on which raft house you are booked into.

faqs.q: Can you swim in Cheow Lan Lake?
faqs.a: Yes, from the raft houses, normally with a life jacket and only close to the raft. Avoid the water during and after heavy rain, when the reservoir level and currents change quickly.

faqs.q: How much does a raft house cost?
faqs.a: Raft houses are sold as per-person packages that usually include the boat transfer, meals and a guide; rates vary by season and by the standard of the raft. Confirm exactly what is included with your operator before booking.

faqs.q: Is Cheow Lan Lake the same as Khao Sok National Park?
faqs.a: The lake is inside Khao Sok National Park but it is a separate zone: the lake and its pier are in Ban Ta Khun District, about 50 km from the main park HQ and the jungle trails.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Cheow Lan Lake?
faqs.a: December to April for calm water and clear trails; May to November for a fuller lake and the lushest forest, though afternoon storms can delay boat trips. Dawn is the best hour in any month.

lake.note: Opening hours, entrance fees and boat operations can change — confirm with the national park or your operator before travelling.

lake.backHome: Back to the full Khao Sok guide

meta.title: Getting to Khao Sok National Park: Airports, Trains & Minivans
meta.description: How to get to Khao Sok National Park from Surat Thani, Phuket, Krabi, Khao Lak and Bangkok — airport transfers, overnight train, minivans, drive times and the park HQ versus lake pier mix-up to avoid.

transport.heading: Getting to Khao Sok: Airports, Trains, Minivans
transport.lead: Khao Sok sits in Surat Thani Province, roughly halfway between the Gulf coast and the Andaman coast, so almost every route starts with one decision: are you heading to the park HQ for the jungle trails, or to the Ratchaprapha Dam pier for Cheow Lan Lake? The two are about 50 km apart.
transport.factsTitle: Khao Sok access at a glance

facts.label: Nearest railway
facts.value: Phun Phin / Surat Thani, Southern Line

facts.label: Without a car
facts.value: Minivan, shared transfer or tour pickup

tableRows: Overnight train to Phun Phin, then about 2 h
Fly to URT, or train plus transfer

sections.h: First: which zone are you going to?
sections.p: Visitors regularly arrive at the wrong entrance. The park HQ in Phanom District (postcode 84250) is the land-based rainforest entrance with the trails, waterfalls and jungle lodges. Cheow Lan Lake is in Ban Ta Khun District (postcode 84230) and is reached by boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam. Check which one your hotel, tour or raft-house booking is in before you set off.
list: Park HQ — Khao Sok village area, Phanom District, 84250
Cheow Lan Lake — Ratchaprapha Dam pier, Ban Ta Khun District, 84230
Plus code for the mapped park entrance: XJHQ+37

sections.p: Surat Thani Airport (URT) is the closest airport, about 70 km from the park. Phuket (HKT) and Krabi (KBV) are 2.5–3 hours away by road and are often cheaper for international flights, which is why many travellers combine Khao Sok with an Andaman coast trip.
list: URT — about 1.5 h by taxi or pre-booked van; some minivans call at the airport
HKT — about 2.5–3 h; shared minivans and private transfers
KBV — about 2.5–3 h; the usual choice for travellers based in Krabi

sections.p: The Southern Line runs from Bangkok to Phun Phin in Surat Thani. An overnight sleeper from Bangkok arrives in the morning, and the onward road transfer takes roughly 1.5–2 hours to the park HQ. It is a comfortable option for long-haul travellers who would rather not take another domestic flight.
list: Bangkok (Krung Thep Aphiwat) to Surat Thani / Phun Phin — overnight sleeper
Phun Phin to the park — about 1.5–2 h by minivan, bus or taxi
Book sleeper berths in advance, especially from November to February

sections.h: By minivan, bus or private transfer
sections.p: Minivans and buses from Surat Thani city, Surat Thani Airport, Phuket, Krabi and Khao Lak are the standard way to arrive. Services cluster in the morning, some drop you at your accommodation, and most operators collect guests from the village for a tour or lake transfer.
list: Cheapest — local bus or minivan with a change in Surat Thani
Most convenient — private transfer or a van arranged by your hotel
Easiest for the lake — a package that collects you and includes the boat

sections.p: If you drive yourself, note that a search for Khao Sok National Park often points to the mapped park entrance rather than the lake pier. Set your destination by district — Phanom for the park HQ, Ban Ta Khun for the dam pier — or use the Plus code, and refuel before leaving town, as petrol stations thin out west of Surat Thani.

The national park entrance fee is paid in cash at the checkpoint: foreign visitors 200/100 THB at the park standard rate, or 300/150 THB in the Ratchaprapha Dam / Cheow Lan Lake special-fee zone; Thai nationals 40/20 THB. Park hours are 06:00–18:00 and overnight stays are only permitted in designated lodges, raft houses or the campsite, so plan to arrive in daylight. From Khao Sok it is straightforward to continue to Khao Lak, Phuket, Krabi or the Gulf islands via Surat Thani and Donsak pier. If prices change, the on-site notice prevails.
list: Bring cash for the park fee
Arrive before dark — roads are unlit and wildlife crosses at dusk
Lake tours normally leave from the dam pier in the morning

transport.faqTitle: Getting to Khao Sok: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: What is the nearest airport to Khao Sok National Park?
faqs.a: Surat Thani Airport (URT), about 70 km and roughly 1.5 hours away by road. Phuket (HKT) and Krabi (KBV) are also used commonly, at about 2.5–3 hours.

faqs.q: Is there a train station near Khao Sok?
faqs.a: The nearest station is Phun Phin in Surat Thani, on the Southern Line, roughly 1.5–2 hours from the park by road. Overnight sleepers from Bangkok arrive there in the morning.

faqs.q: Do I need to rent a car?
faqs.a: No. Minivans, buses, private transfers and tour pickups cover all the usual routes, and most lake packages include both the road transfer and the boat.

faqs.q: How far is Cheow Lan Lake from the park headquarters?
faqs.a: About 50 km, roughly an hour by road, and the two are in different districts. Check which one your booking refers to before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I visit Khao Sok as a day trip from Phuket or Krabi?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is a long day: 2.5–3 hours each way plus travel inside the park. Staying one night, ideally on a Cheow Lan Lake raft house, makes much better use of the trip.

faqs.q: What time does Khao Sok National Park open?
faqs.a: The park is open daily from 06:00 to 18:00, with the entrance fee paid at the checkpoint. Day visitors are expected to leave by closing time and overnight stays are only allowed in designated lodges, raft houses or the campsite. Boats on Cheow Lan Lake may not sail before sunrise or after sunset, so lake transfers happen in daylight.

transport.note: Road times are estimates for normal traffic. During Thai public holidays and the December–April peak season, allow extra time and book transfers in advance.

meta.title: Khao Sok from Phuket & Krabi: Day Trip or Two Days?
meta.description: How to plan Khao Sok National Park from Phuket or Krabi — realistic drive times, what a day trip can and cannot include, two-day and overnight structures, timing rules (park open 06:00–18:00, no lake boats after sunset) and how to avoid the park HQ versus lake pier mix-up.

trips.heading: Khao Sok from Phuket or Krabi: Day Trip or Overnight?
trips.lead: On a map the Andaman coast looks close enough for an easy day trip — and the real distance is just far enough that one day covers only one of the park's two zones. This is planning information only: no operator recommendations, no booking links.

facts.label: Day trip into the lake
facts.value: Not advisable — the pier is another hour by boat each way

facts.label: Realistic minimum
facts.value: One night, at the HQ village or on a raft house

tableRows: A full day of trails; leave the coast around 06:00–06:30
The same day-trip structure, with a slightly shorter drive
Only if you accept about 6–7 h of driving plus about 2 h of boating
Useful when you want to cover both zones
Lake pier to main raft-house area
The lake itself: best with an overnight

sections.h: Day trip or overnight? Start with the two zones
sections.p: Khao Sok is not one place. The park HQ in Phanom District is the rainforest, the trails, the waterfalls and the village; Cheow Lan Lake lies about 50 km west in Ban Ta Khun District and is reached only by boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam. A day trip from the Andaman coast can genuinely deliver the first. It cannot deliver the second without most of the day spent in a vehicle and on the water.
list: HQ day trip — drive, walk, eat, drive back; the lake is not involved
Lake day trip — technically possible, but about 6–7 h of road travel plus about 2 h of boat travel
Lake overnight — the only way to see the water at dawn, when it is calmest

sections.h: A day trip that actually works from Phuket or Krabi
sections.p: Leaving the coast at 06:00 puts you at the HQ checkpoint around 08:30–09:30. That leaves five to six hours of daylight before you need to start back. It is enough for a marked trail to a waterfall and an unhurried lunch in the village, and not enough to add the lake.
list: 06:00 — leave the coast
08:30–09:30 — park HQ: pay the entrance fee and start walking
13:00–14:00 — food and shade in the village
15:00–16:00 — start the return drive
19:00–20:00 — back on the coast

sections.h: Overnight: one night is the working minimum
sections.p: Two structures cover almost every visitor. Sleep in the village by the park HQ and walk trails across two mornings, or sleep on a raft house on the lake and treat the road journey as a one-time cost. If you want both zones, stay one night in each and allow about an hour to transfer between them.
list: One night at the HQ village — two morning walks, no boat involved, lowest cost
One night on the lake — boat in during the afternoon, dawn on the water, out after breakfast
One night in each zone — adds about 1 h of driving in between

sections.h: Inside the park: the clock matters more than the distance
sections.p: Park rules shape an itinerary more than mileage does. The park is open 06:00–18:00, overnight stays are allowed only in designated lodges, licensed raft houses or the campsite, and boats on Cheow Lan Lake may not sail before sunrise or after sunset. Night wildlife spotting happens only in the HQ zone and only with a guide.
list: Keep long drives in daylight — the final roads into the park are unlit
There are no dawn or dusk boat crossings; the last boats run in daylight
Afternoon storms from May to November are the most common reason a plan slips

sections.h: Moving between the coast and the park
sections.p: Shared minivans and buses link Surat Thani, the airports, Phuket, Krabi and Khao Lak with the park area, usually with a change in Surat Thani or the nearest town. Private transfers cost more and remove the change. Self-driving gives the most freedom and the least flexibility in heavy rain. This page does not recommend or book any of them: compare operators yourself, and confirm whether the price includes the lake boat before you pay.
list: Public minivan or bus — cheapest, with a change en route
Private transfer — door to door, priced per vehicle
Self-drive — most freedom for covering both zones, least pleasant in a downpour

sections.h: Three planning mistakes that cause most disappointment
sections.p: Most let-downs come from three errors: treating the park HQ and the lake pier as one place, budgeting travel time at map speed, and assuming a day trip can include the lake. A fourth is booking an overnight without checking whether the transfer boat is included — the difference between arriving at your raft house and standing at a pier at 15:00.
list: The HQ and the lake pier are about 50 km apart and in different districts
Add at least 30% to online drive times in the rainy season
Confirm boats, meals and pick-up points before paying

sections.h: A note on how this page is written
sections.p: This is an independent information page. We do not sell tours, accept commissions, or rank and recommend specific operators, raft houses or hotels. Everything here is planning arithmetic and park rules that you can apply to whichever operator and accommodation you choose.

trips.faqTitle: Khao Sok from Phuket and Krabi: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: Can I see Cheow Lan Lake as a day trip from Phuket?
faqs.a: Not comfortably. From Phuket the pier is 2.5–3 hours each way, and the boat ride to the main raft-house area is about an hour each way — roughly 8 hours of travelling for a few hours on the water, and boats are limited to daylight.

faqs.q: Is a Khao Sok day trip from Krabi worth it?
faqs.a: For the park HQ and the forest trails, yes: the drive is about 2.5 hours each way and a six-hour visit is realistic. For the lake, staying one night makes far better use of the trip.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for both zones?
faqs.a: Two days and one night per zone is comfortable: one night at the HQ village for the trails, then about an hour's drive to the lake pier for a raft-house night.

faqs.q: What time should I leave Phuket or Krabi?
faqs.a: Around 06:00 for a day trip. That puts you at the HQ checkpoint by roughly 08:30–09:30 and leaves enough daylight for the return drive.

faqs.q: Can I stay inside the park overnight?
faqs.a: Yes, but only in designated accommodation: lodges in the HQ village, licensed raft houses on the lake, or the campsite by the visitor centre. Day visitors are expected to leave by the 18:00 closing time.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide?
faqs.a: Not for the marked trails at the HQ. Guided walks are required for night wildlife spotting, cave visits and longer jungle routes, and lake crossings always run with a boat operator.

trips.note: Times are estimates for normal traffic and daylight conditions. Park rules, fees, boat hours and access arrangements can change — if prices change, the on-site notice prevails; confirm current details with the national park or your accommodation before travelling.

trips.backHome: Back to the full Khao Sok guide

meta.title: Khao Sok Entrance Fee 2026: Park & Cheow Lan Lake Rates
meta.description: Khao Sok National Park entrance fees: foreign visitors 200 THB (park standard) or 300 THB (Cheow Lan Lake zone), children 100/150 THB, Thai nationals 40/20 THB. Set by Thailand's DNP — paid in cash at the checkpoint.

entranceFee.heading: Khao Sok National Park Entrance Fees
entranceFee.lead: The national park entrance fee is set by Thailand's Department of National Parks (DNP) and paid in cash at the checkpoint. There are two rate areas: the park standard zone and the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam special-fee zone.
entranceFee.factsTitle: Khao Sok entrance fees at a glance

facts.label: Child rate applies to
facts.value: Ages 3–14, or height up to 140 cm

sections.h: Two fee zones — which one do you pay?
sections.p: Khao Sok is in DNP rate group 2. The main park HQ area (Phanom District) uses the standard rate of 200 THB for foreign adults. The Ratchaprapha Dam / Cheow Lan Lake zone has been a designated special-fee area since 1 May 2024, so most lake visitors pay 300 THB for adults (150 THB for children). Both zones charge the national park entrance fee separately from boats, raft houses and tours.
list: Park HQ & jungle trails (Phanom) — 200 / 100 THB for foreign visitors
Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam (Ban Ta Khun) — 300 / 150 THB for foreign visitors
Thai nationals — 40 / 20 THB in either zone

sections.p: The fee is a day-entry charge to the national park. It covers access to the trails, waterfalls, the visitor centre and the checkpoint area. It does NOT include long-tail boat trips, raft-house stays, guided treks or cave visits — those are priced separately by operators and the lake concessions.

Pay at the national park checkpoint (the ticket window is open about 08:00–16:30). Bring cash in Thai baht; card payment is rarely available at the gate. Keep your receipt — you may be asked for it at trailheads and the dam pier.
list: Cash only at the checkpoint
Ticket window roughly 08:00–16:30
Children 3–14 or under 140 cm pay the child rate

sections.p: Plan a separate budget for the experiences on the water and in the forest. These are not part of the entrance fee and vary by season and operator.
list: Long-tail boat tours on Cheow Lan Lake — per boat or per package
Floating raft-house packages — usually per person, include boat transfer + meals
Guided night safari, cave visits and longer jungle treks — arranged at the HQ
Parking and any village services

entranceFee.faqTitle: Khao Sok entrance fee: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: How much is the Khao Sok entrance fee?
faqs.a: Foreign visitors pay 200 THB (adult) / 100 THB (child) at the park standard rate, or 300 / 150 THB in the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam special-fee zone — the amount most lake visitors pay. Thai nationals pay 40 / 20 THB. The fee is set by the Department of National Parks (DNP) and paid in cash at the checkpoint.

faqs.q: Is the entrance fee the same for the lake and the park HQ?
faqs.a: No. The park HQ (Phanom) uses the standard 200 / 100 THB rate; the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam zone is a designated special-fee area at 300 / 150 THB for foreign visitors. Both are separate from boat and raft-house prices.

faqs.q: Do I pay the fee for a day trip and an overnight stay?
faqs.a: The entrance fee is a day-entry charge. Overnight stays in designated lodges, licensed raft houses or the campsite are priced separately; you still pay the park entrance fee on top.

faqs.q: Can I pay by card?
faqs.a: Usually no — bring cash in Thai baht. The checkpoint and most lake operators do not take cards.

faqs.q: Are there discounts for children or Thai nationals?
faqs.a: Yes. Children aged 3–14 (or under 140 cm) pay the child rate, and Thai nationals pay the much lower domestic rate of 40 / 20 THB.

entranceFee.note: Entrance fees and the special-fee zone are set by the Department of National Parks and can change; the on-site notice at the checkpoint prevails. Confirm current rates with the national park before travelling.

map.lead: The single biggest planning mistake at Khao Sok is heading to the wrong entrance. The park has two very different zones about 50 km apart, in two different districts. Know which one your hotel, tour or raft house is in before you set off.

Lake / dam pier

sections.p: The main land-based entrance: rainforest trails, waterfalls, Rafflesia spotting, the visitor centre and jungle lodges around Khao Sok village. This is where most day hikes and the night safari start.

Trails, waterfalls, village lodges, park HQ

sections.h: Zone 2 · Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam (Ban Ta Khun)
sections.p: The emerald reservoir of limestone karsts, reached only by boat from the Ratchaprapha Dam. This is where the floating raft houses, long-tail boat trips and the famous Three Sisters karsts are. Set your map to Ban Ta Khun, not Phanom.

About 60–65 km (1–1.5 hrs) west of Surat Thani city
Boat pier, raft houses, karsts, cave visits

sections.h: How to navigate without getting lost
sections.p: A search for 'Khao Sok National Park' usually drops the pin on the lake area, not the HQ. Set your destination by district — Phanom for the park HQ, Ban Ta Khun for the dam pier — or use the Plus code XJHQ+37 for the lake. Refuel before leaving town: petrol stations thin out west of Surat Thani.

Lake / dam pier → Ban Ta Khun District

map.faqTitle: Khao Sok map & entrances: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: How far apart are the two Khao Sok entrances?
faqs.a: About 50 km. The park HQ in Phanom District and the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam pier in Ban Ta Khun District are in different districts and take roughly an hour to drive between.

faqs.q: Which entrance do I need for the lake?
faqs.a: For Cheow Lan Lake you need the Ratchaprapha Dam pier in Ban Ta Khun District, not the park HQ in Phanom. The lake is reached only by boat from the dam.

faqs.q: What does the Plus code XJHQ+37 point to?
faqs.a: The maps pin (Plus code XJHQ+37) marks the Cheow Lan Lake / Ratchaprapha Dam area in Ban Ta Khun District — not the park HQ. Use it when navigating to the lake.

faqs.q: Can I visit both zones in one day?
faqs.a: Yes, but it is tight. The zones are about an hour apart; most visitors pick one zone per day, or stay one night in each.

map.note: Distances are estimates for normal driving. During Thai holidays and the December–April peak, allow extra time and confirm your exact destination before setting off.

meta.title: Best Time to Visit Khao Sok: Dry vs Green Season
meta.description: Khao Sok has two broad seasons: the dry window (Dec–Apr) is most comfortable and popular, while the green season (May–Nov) is lushest with active wildlife. The lake is scenic year-round; Rafflesia peaks in the dry season (Nov–Mar).

bestTime.heading: Best Time to Visit Khao Sok National Park
bestTime.lead: There is no bad month, but the experience changes a lot. The dry season is easiest and most comfortable; the green season is wild, wet and lush. Match the season to what you want to see.
bestTime.factsTitle: Khao Sok seasons at a glance

sections.h: Dry season (Dec – Apr): easiest & most popular
sections.p: Lower rainfall, clearer trails and calmer lake water make this the most comfortable time. It is also the busiest and most humid, so book raft houses well ahead. This is the Rafflesia peak (Nov–Mar), when the giant flower is most likely to be in bloom.
list: Calm lake, clear trails, easier trekking
Rafflesia kerrii most likely (Nov–Mar)
Busiest and priciest for lake stays — book early

sections.p: Heavy monsoon rain fills the lake and makes the forest at its lushest, with the most spectacular waterfalls and active wildlife. Trails flood easily and leeches thrive — but it is also quieter and greener, and this is NOT the Rafflesia peak.
list: Fuller lake, running waterfalls, active wildlife
Afternoon storms common — plan boat transfers for the morning
Fewer crowds; bring proper rain gear

sections.p: December to February is the mildest and driest; March to April stays dry but hotter; May to October is the wettest, with the lake at its fullest around September–October; November bridges the seasons and often brings the first Rafflesia.
list: Dec–Feb: cool, dry, comfortable
Mar–Apr: dry, hot, humid
May–Oct: wet, lush, full lake
Nov: transition, Rafflesia starts

sections.p: Year-round essentials are rain gear, insect repellent and grippy shoes — this is Thailand's wettest spot. Add a jacket for dawn boat trips and a dry bag for the lake.
list: Dry season: light layers, sun protection, water
Green season: rain jacket, leech socks, quick-dry clothing
Any month: repellent, rain gear, reusable water bottle

bestTime.faqTitle: Best time to visit Khao Sok: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Khao Sok?
faqs.a: December to April is driest and most comfortable, with December–February the mildest. March–April is dry but hotter. The lake is beautiful in any month.

faqs.q: When can I see the Rafflesia flower?
faqs.a: The giant Rafflesia kerrii is most likely in bloom during the dry season, roughly November to March, and is best seen with a certified guide deep in the forest.

faqs.q: Is the green season worth visiting?
faqs.a: Yes — the forest is at its lushest, waterfalls run hard and wildlife is active, with fewer crowds. Just expect afternoon storms and bring rain gear; boat transfers are best in the morning.

faqs.q: Is Khao Sok busy?
faqs.a: The dry season (Dec–Apr) and Thai public holidays are the busiest. Arrive early for parking and calmer lake water; the green season is much quieter.

bestTime.note: Weather patterns can shift; this is a general guide based on southern Thailand's two monsoon systems. Check the forecast close to your trip.
bestTime.relatedTitle: Plan the rest of your trip
bestTime.backHome: Back to the full Khao Sok guide

meta.title: Jungle Trekking in Khao Sok: Trails, Guides & Wildlife
meta.description: Khao Sok jungle trekking: self-guided short trails at the park HQ, plus guided walks for Rafflesia, caves, waterfalls and the night safari. What to see, what to bring and how to trek safely in one of Earth's oldest rainforests.

trekking.heading: Jungle Trekking in Khao Sok
trekking.lead: Khao Sok's rainforest is around 160 million years old — older than the Amazon. Trails range from easy boardwalk strolls to guided jungle routes, and the wildlife includes gibbons, hornbills, tapirs and, with luck, wild elephants.
trekking.factsTitle: Khao Sok trekking at a glance

sections.p: The park HQ area has short, marked nature trails and boardwalks suitable for families. Longer jungle routes, cave visits and Rafflesia walks require a certified guide arranged at the HQ.
list: Easy: boardwalks, riverside trails, canopy viewpoints
Moderate: waterfall trails, longer forest loops
Guided only: Nam Talu Cave, Rafflesia sites, deep jungle

sections.p: Thailand's largest flower, Rafflesia kerrii (up to 80 cm across), blooms briefly and is best seen with a guide in the dry season (Nov–Mar). Waterfalls run hardest in the green season. Never pick plants or flowers.
list: Rafflesia kerrii — dry season, guided only
Waterfalls — fullest May–Oct
Stay on trails; do not disturb wildlife

sections.p: Night wildlife spotting happens only in the HQ zone and only with a guide. You may hear gibbons settle, spot nocturnal birds and, rarely, larger mammals near the forest edge. Keep quiet and keep your distance.
list: HQ zone only, guided
Bring a red-light torch if allowed
No flash photography; never feed wildlife

sections.p: The forest is hot, humid and leech-prone year-round. Cover up, treat water and let someone know your route.
list: Long trousers, long socks (against leeches), grippy shoes
Rain gear, drinking water, insect repellent
Keep 50 m+ from elephants; follow your guide

trekking.faqTitle: Khao Sok trekking: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: Do I need a guide to trek in Khao Sok?
faqs.a: Short marked trails near the HQ are self-guided. Certified guides are required for cave visits, Rafflesia spotting, longer jungle routes and the night safari — arrange them at the park HQ.

faqs.q: Can I see Rafflesia on my own?
faqs.a: No — Rafflesia kerrii grows deep in the forest and is best seen with a certified guide, mostly in the dry season (Nov–Mar). Check bloom status at the HQ before you go.

faqs.q: Is trekking safe?
faqs.a: Yes with care. Stay on trails, cover up against leeches, carry water and repellent, and keep a safe distance from wildlife — at least 50 m from elephants. Night walks are guided only.

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be?
faqs.a: Easy boardwalk and riverside trails suit most fitness levels. Waterfall and jungle routes need more stamina, especially in the heat and after rain.

trekking.note: Trail conditions and guide availability change with the season; confirm at the park HQ and follow ranger advice on the day.

meta.title: Floating Bungalows on Cheow Lan Lake: How to Book & What to Expect
meta.description: Cheow Lan Lake floating raft houses: how to book, what packages include (boat transfer, meals, guide), prices per person, the best season, and on-the-lake tips for an overnight stay in Khao Sok.

bungalows.heading: Floating Bungalows on Cheow Lan Lake
bungalows.lead: Sleeping on the water is the signature Khao Sok experience. Floating raft houses are run by lake-licensed operators and sold as packages rather than plain rooms — usually including the boat transfer from the dam, meals and a local guide.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Cheow Lan Lake, reached by boat from Ratchaprapha Dam

facts.label: Payment
facts.value: Cash; cards rare on the lake

sections.h: What a floating raft house is
sections.p: Raft houses are wooden lodges on pontoons, moored in calm coves of the lake. They range from simple shared huts to smarter private rafts, but all share the same magic: mist on still water at dawn and the lake to yourself before the day-trippers arrive.
list: On the water, not on land
Simple to comfortable; all are rustic
Dawn mist and karst reflections are the highlight

sections.p: A day trip is possible, but the boat ride from the dam to the main raft-house area takes about an hour each way, so much of the day is travel. One night is what most visitors remember; two nights adds kayaking, a jungle trek and a cave or waterfall stop.
list: Day trip — cruise, viewpoint, lunch, back by late afternoon
One night — sunrise on the water, night jungle sounds
Two nights — adds kayaking, trek and cave/waterfall

sections.p: Packages are usually per person and include the boat transfer from the dam, meals, life jackets and a local guide. Rates vary with the season and the standard of the raft, so confirm exactly what is included before paying. Book well ahead in the dry season and on Thai holidays.
list: Confirm boat transfer, meals and guide are included
Bring cash — cards are rarely accepted on the lake
Book ahead for Dec–Apr and holiday weekends

sections.p: Life jackets are mandatory on the boats and swimming is only safe close to the raft. The reservoir is deep and weather can change fast in the afternoon; there is no night boating.
list: Wear the life jacket for the whole crossing
Swim only near the raft, never far out
Mobile signal fades; tell someone your plan

bungalows.faqTitle: Cheow Lan Lake raft houses: frequently asked questions

faqs.q: How much does a raft house cost?
faqs.a: Raft houses are sold as per-person packages that usually include the boat transfer, meals and a guide. Rates vary by season and by the standard of the raft, so confirm exactly what is included with your operator before booking.

faqs.q: Can I book a raft house without a tour?
faqs.a: You can drive to the Ratchaprapha Dam pier and arrange a boat, but in practice most visitors book a package because boats are shared and there is no reliable walk-up ticket window at the pier.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim?
faqs.a: Yes, from the raft houses, normally with a life jacket and only close to the raft. Avoid the water during and after heavy rain, when the reservoir level and currents change quickly.

faqs.q: What is the best season for a raft-house stay?
faqs.a: December to April brings calmer water and clearer trails; May to November is lusher but afternoon storms can delay boats. Either way, book ahead in the dry season.

bungalows.note: Raft-house operations, prices and boat hours can change — confirm with your operator and the national park before travelling.
